_comment: Instance data for core/scripts/open-items.py and core/helpers/open-items-gate.cjs. Each entry declares a CLASS of open items the operator approved once for good: the session-start list prints them as `standing` in their own group, and the first reply handles them and reports what was done instead of asking "n I can handle — shall I?". Only items the agent could handle anyway (`ai`) or that nobody classified yet (`?`) can become `standing`; an item the data gives to a person stays `human`. An `ai` item that matches no class is still asked about. No file, or an empty list, keeps the old behaviour.
_fields: name: label printed with each item · kind: request | PR · scope: regex on the request's topic folder or the PR's repo (optional) · audience: tokens, one of which the request's audience must name — its file's `audience:` field or the `AN <who>:` of a LOG heading (optional; never matches a PR) · title: regex on the item text (optional) · excludes: regexes on the item text that keep an item OUT of the class — what stays gated whatever the class says (release, tag, pin, live writes) · granted: the operator's words in quotes plus the date they were said, "..." YYYY-MM-DD. An entry without both is refused with a line at session start — the agent cannot grant itself a standing approval.

_example_classes.name: shared-memory requests addressed to this machine
_example_classes.granted: "<the operator's words that granted it>" YYYY-MM-DD
